contract: CBWeb3 Scenario B — Hub-and-spoke settlement (discovery and corridor registry)

vectors.title: Hub contract discovery with no credentials
vectors.description: The credential-free entry point. This route is registered on EVERY Scenario B gateway regardless of which AMM services are wired, so it is the cheapest probe of whether a host speaks Scenario B at all.

preconditions.session: none — no cookie, no bearer token

vectors.notes: The addresses are public on-chain data, which is why the endpoint needs no credential. This operation declares a 200 and nothing else — not even a 500.

vectors.title: Hub currencies come back WRAPPED, not as a bare array
vectors.description: Registered fiat symbols mapped to their Hub W-token address and the Central Bank that proposed them.
vectors.notes: Spec divergence, mirrored to the implementation. The platform document declares the 200 body as a bare JSON array; the delivered handler returns {"currencies": [...]}. A client that iterates the response directly gets nothing. The same divergence applies to /api/v2/amm/pairs and /api/v2/bridge/positions.

vectors.title: Pairs listing is the ONLY supported source of a pool_pair value
vectors.description: Five incompatible pair-naming conventions appear across the delivered artefacts and none is documented as canonical (catalogued in Toolbox/DIVERGENCES.md). Treat pair_id as an opaque string and never construct one.
vectors.notes: The conventions seen in the platform's own artefacts are tCeBM_BRL-tCeBM_ARS, W-tCeBM_BRL/W-tCeBM_ARS and W-BRL-ARS. A client that builds one of these itself will match nothing. Served from the gateway's pair_proposals table with no on-chain RPC, and wrapped in a pairs key contrary to the platform document.

vectors.title: Pool status must read ACTIVE before any swap
vectors.description: The liveness gate. EMPTY means no side has been seeded; PENDING_COUNTERPART means one Central Bank has committed and the other has not.
vectors.notes: pool_status is the one recovered vocabulary the contract publishes as a real enum (EMPTY | PENDING_COUNTERPART | ACTIVE), because the gateway derives it exhaustively from the two reserves and gates swaps on it. Bridge state and swap status remain free strings by contrast — the platform commits to no vocabulary for those.

vectors.title: Circuit breaker must not be halted before a swap
vectors.description: Public. A halted breaker makes a cross-currency swap fail with 422 CIRCUIT_BREAKER_HALTED, so a client checks this first.
vectors.notes: ALWAYS send pair explicitly — see registry-edge-01. The states the delivered gateway emits are LIVE, HALTED and RESUME_PENDING; the contract leaves the field a free string because the platform declares no enum. Note the gateway reports a read failure as 500 rather than fabricating a benign LIVE.

vectors.title: Register a hub currency — 201, not the documented 200
vectors.description: Step 0 of opening a corridor. A Central Bank registers its own currency on the hub, which records the corresponding W-token.

preconditions.session: central_bank cookie for the currency's own issuing Central Bank

vectors.notes: Spec divergence: the platform document declares 200 with no schema; the delivered handler returns 201 with the service result. proposer_cb must be the caller — the field is validated, not merely echoed.

vectors.title: Propose a pair — the Central Bank of token A only
vectors.description: Step 1 of the two-Central-Bank corridor opening.

preconditions.session: central_bank cookie for the Central Bank that ISSUES token A

vectors.notes: OMIT amm_address unless you know exactly why you are setting it. When omitted the service deploys a dedicated per-pair AMM bound to (token_a, token_b). Supplying a shared or bootstrap AMM address mis-binds the pool and makes every subsequent swap on it wrong in a way that does not surface as an error here.

vectors.title: Confirm the pair — the Central Bank of token B activates the corridor
vectors.description: Step 2. On success the pair becomes ACTIVE and liquidity can be seeded.

preconditions.session: central_bank cookie for the Central Bank that ISSUES token B

vectors.notes: Note the asymmetry: propose returns 201 and confirm returns 200. An ACTIVE pair is not yet a tradeable pool — GET /api/v2/amm/pool/{pair}/status will still read EMPTY until both Central Banks have committed liquidity.

vectors.title: Re-registering an existing currency symbol is 409
vectors.description: The registry rejects a duplicate symbol or a token address that is already registered.
vectors.notes: Undeclared upstream; observed in the delivered handler and published in the contract. Mind the key name: the registry family returns its machine-readable code under code, the AMM and swap family returns it under error_code, and the /api/v1 surface has no code at all. Three spellings on one platform. A duplicate token_address under a different symbol yields TOKEN_ALREADY_REGISTERED instead.

vectors.title: Removing an unknown currency is 404 CURRENCY_NOT_FOUND
vectors.description: The cleanest unknown-currency assertion on the whole Scenario B surface, because it is the one place the platform commits to a distinct not-found code.
vectors.notes: Only the Central Bank that registered a currency may remove it. A successful removal returns 200 with NO response body declared.

vectors.title: Proposing a pair you do not issue token A for is 403
vectors.description: Sovereignty check. A Central Bank cannot open a corridor on another Central Bank's token.

preconditions.session: central_bank cookie for a Central Bank that does NOT issue token A

vectors.notes: The mirror check on confirm carries code NOT_CENTRAL_BANK_OF_TOKEN_B. Note that the platform's shared 403 response is described as 'requires CENTRAL_BANK role', which is inaccurate for the routes the router actually gates on commercial_bank — the description is shared, the behaviour is not.

vectors.title: Confirming an already-active pair is 409
vectors.description: Corridor activation is a one-way transition.

preconditions.session: central_bank cookie for the Central Bank of token B

vectors.notes: Re-proposing an existing pair yields 409 PAIR_ALREADY_EXISTS on the propose route. Both codes are undeclared upstream and recovered from the delivered handler.

vectors.title: Confirming a pair that was never proposed is 404
vectors.description: Confirm operates on an existing proposal; there is no create-on-confirm path.

vectors.title: Pool status for an unavailable pool is 422, not the documented 404
vectors.description: Divergence between the platform document and the delivered handler, mirrored to the implementation because the platform surface wins.
vectors.notes: The contract declares BOTH 404 (because the platform document does) and 422 (because the handler emits it). A client must tolerate either; a conformance runner should assert 422 against a live gateway and accept 404 only from a mock served straight off the upstream document.

vectors.title: Circuit breaker status with no pair reports a pair nobody trades
vectors.description: A trap with real settlement consequences. The pair query parameter is undeclared upstream and, when omitted, the delivered service falls back to the literal string BRL-USD — which is not a pair identifier any corridor in this network uses.
vectors.notes: A client that omits pair can receive a healthy LIVE for a pair it is not trading while the pair it IS trading is halted, and will then be surprised by a 422 CIRCUIT_BREAKER_HALTED on the swap. Assert the returned pair equals the pair you asked about, and treat a mismatch as a failed pre-flight check. Note BRL-USD is a fourth pair-name spelling, distinct from all three in registry-hp-03.

vectors.title: Sovereign wrapped-token supply is the only place decimals are stated
vectors.description: How much of one Central Bank's domestic reserves are currently bridged to the hub. Deliberately scoped to a single currency — a network-wide total would mix currencies and double-count the same backing.

preconditions.gateway: a Central Bank gateway with a hub RPC configured

vectors.notes: This decimals field is the ONLY decimals count stated anywhere in the entire CBWeb3 surface, and it describes a Hub W-token — not tCeBM and not fCeBM on a spoke. Do not generalise it into a scale factor for /api/v1 amounts. A hub RPC failure here is a 502, never a fabricated zero.
